data.description:
## Context

Gerrit change 2169 passed LLM review and CI, but the reviewer recorded four non-blocking hardening opportunities for the new explicit tracker-footprint command.

The primary correctness question is an alternates-backed shared clone: the mounted pack layer currently measures only the primary common object database and can report near-zero while objects reside in alternates. The report labels the object database shared and the definition says primary, so this is not a blocker for the fresh-clone incident measurement, but the mounted interpretation should be made harder to misuse.

The other findings are portable test gaps: allocation-ratio assertions depend on filesystem block charging, and the unavailable-allocation text plus bad-argument exit-2 paths lack direct coverage.

## Plan

- Decide and document whether mounted pack reporting should enumerate alternate object databases or retain primary-only scope with an explicit unavailable/non-exclusive interpretation.
- Add a real shared-clone fixture that pins the chosen semantics without double-counting shared objects.
- Replace filesystem-ratio assumptions with deterministic injected/stat capability assertions.
- Cover text rendering when allocation is unavailable and CLI parse failure exit code 2.
- Preserve the command as opt-in, read-only, unscheduled, non-gating, and threshold-free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Alternates-backed mounted reporting cannot be mistaken for an exclusive whole-object-store pack measurement.
- [ ] Shared-clone coverage proves the chosen ownership and deduplication semantics.
- [ ] Allocation-unavailable text and bad-argument exit 2 have direct tests.
- [ ] Tests do not depend on a particular filesystem block allocation policy.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and focused tests pass.
data.title: Harden tracker-footprint shared-clone semantics and edge-path coverage
